# Every number

<!-- Generated by tools/docs.ts from data/ and calc/. Do not edit: change the data and run `pnpm docs`. -->

Every number Phosphoros publishes, where it comes from and how it is computed. Inputs are read from
[`data/`](../data/); everything else is derived by [`calc/`](../calc/) from them. Run
`pnpm calc --only <id>` to reproduce any one of them, or `pnpm calc --set <id>=<value>` to change an
assumption and see what follows.

Basis: **Physics** is measurement or established physics. **Precedent** is shown in the real world,
or taken from a published study, and cited. **Invented** is a breakthrough the plan assumes.
**Design choice** is a size, count or date the plan picks. A computed number carries the weakest basis
among what it is computed from: computed by physics from an invented input, it is marked Invented.

## Checks

Each check is a law of physics or a requirement of the plan, tested on every run.

| Check | Result | Detail | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="check-veil-v2-hovers"></a>**Version 2: a statite Veil 137,000 km sunward of Venus can hover** | Fails: open problem `veil-statite` | Light pressure (0.0174 m/s²) and Venus's gravity both point toward Venus; the shade falls with 0.0347 m/s² and reaches Venus in about 1 d. | [model/veil.ts:91](../calc/src/model/veil.ts#L91) |
| <a id="check-veil-hovers"></a>**A station exists where gravity, light pressure and orbital motion balance on the Veil** | Pass | At 1.11 × 10⁶ km sunward of Venus the forces on a Veil with a lightness of 0.0077 balance. The point is unstable along the Sun line, so holding it takes constant trimming, by tilting slats, which the model does not size. | [model/veil.ts:262](../calc/src/model/veil.ts#L262) |
| <a id="check-veil-leak-fits"></a>**Gaps and closed slats together leak no more than the Veil may** | Pass | Gaps of 0.05% plus 0.03% through the closed slats, against the 0.1% the closed Veil may let through. | [model/veil.ts:324](../calc/src/model/veil.ts#L324) |
| <a id="check-exhaust-fits-venus"></a>**The tiles fit in the band between the drop zones, the lit ones on the side the Lattice sees** | Pass | The lit tiles throw out 2.2 × 10²⁰ W at 1.3 MW/m², and only 50% of them are lit at once, so the tiles cover 72% of Venus: 83% of the band within 60° of the equator, which leaves the poles to the falling ice. | [model/exhaust.ts:354](../calc/src/model/exhaust.ts#L354) |
| <a id="check-second-law"></a>**The heat pumps are charged more than the reversible work** | Pass | The pumps reach 50% of the Carnot limit, so the model charges 1.09 × 10²⁸ J of work for 5.3 × 10²⁶ J of heat, more than the 2.0 × 10²⁷ J even a reversible pump would need if every joule left from 737 K. | [model/exhaust.ts:449](../calc/src/model/exhaust.ts#L449) |
| <a id="check-exhaust-spares-veil"></a>**The Exhaust's light adds little to the sunlight the Veil turns away** | Pass | Seen from Venus the Veil is 0.68° in radius, so the lit tiles send it 0.007% of their light: 1.5 × 10¹⁶ W at the Exhaust's peak, 5.1% of the 3.0 × 10¹⁷ W of sunlight it turns away. It pushes the Veil toward the Sun, against the sunlight, and the slats that trim its station take it up. | [model/exhaust.ts:539](../calc/src/model/exhaust.ts#L539) |
| <a id="check-exhaust-pump-photons"></a>**Each pump photon leaves the tile with room for the heat the model has it carry** | Pass | Pumped at 2.5 µm, below the tiles' 0.54 eV bandgap, each photon leaves at least 0.54 eV plus the heat of the tile it crossed. From the hottest starting air a joule of pumping light can carry 0.26 J of heat; the model has it carry 0.12 J, and less as the air cools. | [model/exhaust.ts:616](../calc/src/model/exhaust.ts#L616) |
| <a id="check-graphite-for-caps"></a>**The Forges make the cap graphite before sealing ends** | Pass | 4.6 × 10¹⁷ kg of graphite by the end of sealing; the caps need 2.5 × 10¹⁷ kg. | [model/forges.ts:155](../calc/src/model/forges.ts#L155) |
| <a id="check-ice-arrives"></a>**The last Brick reaches Venus while the pumps still run** | Pass | Launches run from 9 October 2033 to 7 January 2034. The slowest transfer takes 410 d, and the last Brick falls into the air on 23 January 2035, before the pumps stop with the last caps on 1 September 2036. Its heat is the pumps' to take out. | [model/ice.ts:843](../calc/src/model/ice.ts#L843) |
| <a id="check-ceres-ground-heat"></a>**Ceres's surface can radiate the heat left on the ground** | Pass | All the heat made at Ceres is 6.6 times what its whole surface could radiate at 1,500 K (8.0 × 10¹⁷ W), so the Crown sheds it in space; the barrels leave 6.3 × 10¹⁵ W on the ground, radiators over 0.79% of the surface. | [model/ceres.ts:769](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L769) |
| <a id="check-ceres-receiver-cooling"></a>**Ceres's receivers shed heat no faster than a cooled surface already does** | Pass | At 40 MW/m² each square metre of receiver hands 10 MW/m² to its coolant, against the 10 MW/m² ITER's divertor is built to carry; left to radiate it alone, a receiver would reach 3,100 K. | [model/ceres.ts:780](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L780) |
| <a id="check-crown-orbit"></a>**The Crown stays deep inside Ceres's Hill sphere, and the recoil cannot shake it off** | Pass | The Crown circles at 1,190 km and its fins reach 2,100 km, well inside half of Ceres's 220,000 km Hill radius, where orbits around a small body stay bound; Ceres's recoil, 9.1 × 10⁻⁷ m/s², is small beside its 0.014 m/s² pull even at the fins' edge. | [model/ceres.ts:791](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L791) |
| <a id="check-crown-tethers"></a>**Carbon-fibre tethers can hang from the Crown to Ceres's surface** | Pass | Summed from the surface to the Crown, Ceres's net pull on a tether is 59 kJ/kg, against the 3.9 MJ/kg carbon fibre holds at full strength; hanging the 8.1 × 10¹¹ kg of cables and holding the beams' 2.8 × 10¹⁰ N push takes 1.8 × 10¹⁰ kg of fibre. | [model/ceres.ts:804](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L804) |
| <a id="check-ceres-ready-in-time"></a>**The first launch waits for Ceres's factories, whose seed leaves with the Foundry's** | Pass | The seed leaves Earth on 1 October 2028, with the Foundry's once Ouroboros-0 has passed, and lands on 16 January 2030; doubling every 45 d, the factories finish the 6.5 × 10¹³ kg of Railheads and Crown on 2 June 2033, against a first launch on 9 October 2033. | [model/ceres.ts:815](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L815) |
| <a id="check-railheads-within-lattice"></a>**The Lattice can power the Railheads** | Pass | Throwing 1.0 × 10¹⁸ kg in 0.25 yr takes 6.3 × 10¹⁸ W, which Ceres's receivers make from 8.4 × 10¹⁸ W of the Lattice's 2.2 × 10²⁰ W. | [model/ceres.ts:828](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L828) |
| <a id="check-ceres-clear-of-jupiter"></a>**Ceres's new orbit stays clear of Jupiter** | Pass | At its new aphelion Ceres stays 2.18 AU inside Jupiter's closest approach to the Sun, 6.1 of Jupiter's Hill radii against the 2√3 that keeps two orbits from meeting; its Tisserand parameter falls from 3.31 to 3.31, still above the 3 below which Jupiter takes control. | [model/ceres.ts:839](../calc/src/model/ceres.ts#L839) |
| <a id="check-foundry-affords-veil"></a>**Building the Veil costs the Foundry no more than one doubling** | Pass | The Foundry stands still for 9.8 d to build the 5.4 × 10¹¹ kg Veil, whose last parts leave Mercury on 16 September 2032; one doubling is 60 d. | [model/foundry.ts:419](../calc/src/model/foundry.ts#L419) |
| <a id="check-foundry-size"></a>**The Foundry stops growing at the size that finishes the Lattice and the hardware at Venus soonest** | Pass | After 28 doublings the 2.7 × 10¹⁴ kg Foundry builds the 1.2 × 10¹⁴ kg Lattice in 39 d and the 1.9 × 10¹⁴ kg of hardware at Venus in 61 d: both done 1780 days after landing, against 1821 with one doubling fewer and 1790 with one more. | [model/foundry.ts:435](../calc/src/model/foundry.ts#L435) |
| <a id="check-aegis-structure"></a>**The Foundry can build the structure that holds the Aegis coil together** | Pass | The coil's field pulls on its winding with 1.2 × 10¹¹ N; holding it takes at least 2.0 × 10¹¹ kg of carbon fibre at full strength, 0.063 days of the full Foundry's output against the 60 d of one doubling. | [model/shield.ts:338](../calc/src/model/shield.ts#L338) |
| <a id="check-forges-on-seas"></a>**The Forges start once the liquid CO₂ seas are there for good** | Pass | The Forges float on the seas from April 2035; the Clear Rain begins for good on January 2035. | [model/trajectory.ts:586](../calc/src/model/trajectory.ts#L586) |
| <a id="check-traj-heat-books"></a>**The simulation's heat books balance: it lifts every joule it counts in** | Pass | The Exhaust lifts 7.3 × 10²⁶ J: Venus's 5.3 × 10²⁶ J, less the 1.6 × 10²¹ J still held by the CO₂ the Frost Towers leave in the air, plus 2.0 × 10²⁶ J that enters while the pumps run. The two sides agree to rounding. This confirms the simulation's own bookkeeping; a heat source the simulation leaves out cannot show here. | [model/trajectory.ts:594](../calc/src/model/trajectory.ts#L594) |
| <a id="check-frozen-before-sealing"></a>**The seas are frozen through before the last caps are sealed** | Pass | The simulated seas are frozen through on 30 April 2036, leaving 120 d to the last cap on 1 September 2036: the crawler-rafts must lay 1.2 × 10⁶ km²/d. | [model/trajectory.ts:686](../calc/src/model/trajectory.ts#L686) |
| <a id="check-frost-before-sealing"></a>**The Frost Towers finish before the last caps are sealed** | Pass | The simulated Frost Towers finish on 26 June 2036; the last caps are sealed on 1 September 2036. | [model/trajectory.ts:744](../calc/src/model/trajectory.ts#L744) |
| <a id="check-genesis-by-deadline"></a>**Seeded life greens the seas by the deadline** | Pass | Seeding waits for the oxygen (30 September 2036) and for the seas to hold their pH (1 December 2036), so it begins on 1 December 2036; doubling every 1 d, the cells reach bloom density on 12 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036. | [model/trajectory.ts:806](../calc/src/model/trajectory.ts#L806) |
| <a id="check-earth-like-by-deadline"></a>**The simulated atmosphere is Earth-like by the deadline** | Pass | The day-by-day simulation reaches Earth-like conditions on 30 September 2036, 92 d before the 31 December 2036 deadline. The chimneys, not the power, set the pace on 51 d of it. | [model/trajectory.ts:817](../calc/src/model/trajectory.ts#L817) |
| <a id="check-ozone-model-earth"></a>**The ozone model, run on Earth's air, gives Earth's ozone column** | Pass | 280 DU against 279 DU from a three-dimensional model of the pre-industrial Earth, within a quarter either way, with nothing fitted. | [model/ozone.ts:257](../calc/src/model/ozone.ts#L257) |
| <a id="check-ozone-shield-in-time"></a>**The ozone shields the land before the deadline** | Pass | One day of sunlight makes 49.9 DU, easily measured. The column reaches 185 DU on 2 December 2036, 91 d after the Veil opens, so lichens and mosses go onto land from 2 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036. | [model/ozone.ts:391](../calc/src/model/ozone.ts#L391) |
| <a id="check-energy-closes"></a>**The energy budget closes: supply covers demand** | Pass | The Lattice beams 2.2 × 10²⁸ J from full power to the deadline, against 1.6 × 10²⁸ J the plan needs: 30% spare. | [model/budget.ts:86](../calc/src/model/budget.ts#L86) |
